title: Request Routing
description: Learn request routing patterns in API Gateways for directing traffic to the right services.

data.text: Request routing is the core function of an API Gateway. Amazon Route 53, AWS API Gateway, and Kong all support dynamic routing based on path, headers, query parameters, and even request content.

data.title: Common Routing Approaches
items: Header-based routing: Route based on X-API-Version or X-Client-Type
Query parameter routing: Route based on ?version=v2
Content-based routing: Route based on request body (rare, expensive)

data.text: Advanced gateways support dynamic routing for canary deployments and blue-green deployments. You can route a percentage of traffic to a new version while monitoring for errors before fully rolling out.

data.title: Canary Routing
data.text: Route 5% of traffic to a new service version. If error rates are normal, gradually increase to 100%. This reduces deployment risk significantly.

data.title: Example: Kong Route Configuration
data.code: Configure path-based and header-based routing in Kong.

services:
  - name: user-service-v1
    url: http://user-service-v1:8080
    routes:
      - name: user-v1-route
        paths: ["/api/v1/users"]
        methods: ["GET"]

  - name: user-service-v2
    url: http://user-service-v2:8080
    routes:
      - name: user-v2-route
        paths: ["/api/v2/users"]
        methods: ["GET"]
      - name: user-v2-header
        paths: ["/api/users"]
        methods: ["GET"]
        headers:
          X-API-Version: v2

items.question: Should I use path-based or header-based routing?
items.answer: Path-based is simpler and more RESTful. Header-based is useful for versioning without changing URLs or for A/B testing.

items.question: How do I handle routing failures?
items.answer: Return a 502 Bad Gateway or 503 Service Unavailable. Configure fallback routes if available. Use circuit breakers for downstream failures.

items.question: Can routing be dynamic?
items.answer: Yes. Kong, AWS API Gateway, and Netflix Zuul support dynamic routing based on runtime conditions, enabling canary deployments and feature flags.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Routing directs requests to the correct backend service
Path and header routing are the most common
Always configure fallbacks for routing failures
data.takeaway: Effective request routing simplifies client code and enables advanced deployment strategies.
